events.description: Framed Blackjack as a supervised learning problem and generated training data with a game simulator, targeting a model that maximizes long-term winnings.
Explored the data for correlations and outliers, then selected the key features: the dealer's visible card, the starting and final hands, and the actions taken.
Cleaned the dataset and broke each game into individual decisions, encoding categorical variables with one-hot and ordinal encoding.
Designed three candidate architectures — XGBoost, a feedforward network, and a recurrent network — and split the data into training, validation, and test sets.
Trained all three models to predict the optimal action for a given game state, applying feature scaling and encoding across the pipeline.
Compared the models on accuracy, confusion matrices, and feature importance to understand each one's strengths and weaknesses.
Tuned hyperparameters and refined the network architectures to push prediction accuracy higher on the toughest game states.
Selected the best-performing model on the evaluation metrics and finalized it for testing.
Kicked off the Smart Pet Feeder as cloud team lead, setting the vision and organizing the work around Scrum with the wider team.

events.milestone: Requirement Gathering and Cloud Architecture Design
events.description: Gathered requirements from stakeholders and designed the cloud architecture for scalability, data processing, and real-time feeding-data sync.
Set up the cloud infrastructure with a focus on availability and security, handling user data, activity logs, and feeding schedules.
Built the backend API connecting the feeders to the cloud, including user authentication and endpoints for feeding schedules and health insights.
Integrated the Arduino hardware with the cloud API to enable remote feeding, working through the hardware-to-cloud challenges with the IoT team.
Finished the real-time integration between the cloud API and the devices, ensuring reliable two-way data sync for accurate feeding schedules.
Worked with the frontend and IoT teams to test end to end, fixing issues and tightening the API so feeder and cloud stayed in sync.
Deployed to production and tested scalability, tuning the infrastructure to handle a growing number of users and devices in real time.
Wrote the user guides and API documentation covering setup, feeding-schedule configuration, and troubleshooting for owners and stakeholders.

title: Pnta 🎉

events.description: Designed the experience for both the app and the manager platform — wireframes, user flows, and UI mockups — and planned a scalable microservice architecture.
Built the backend foundation for both platforms: databases, APIs, and microservices with flexible communication and central user-data management.
Built the manager platform — an admin interface for overseeing user activity, generating reports, and managing system data, with built-in alerting and notifications.
Started the app itself, implementing registration, login, and venue discovery, and wiring up the APIs that sync data with the backend.
Connected the frontend to the backend APIs for a smooth cross-platform experience, with real-time updates shared between the app and manager platform.

title: BEUMER Group - Smart Vision 📦

events.description: Kicked off by building domain knowledge and exploring the available datasets — essential for understanding both the problem and our partners' constraints.
Evaluated several computer vision frameworks and chose a YOLOv9-based architecture for its balance of speed, accuracy, and real-time inference.
Preprocessed the raw image data — normalization, labeling, and augmentation — with a focus on class balance and stronger generalization.
Added an active-learning loop so the model could flag uncertain predictions for human review, making each training cycle more efficient on edge cases.
Evaluated the model on standard CV metrics (mAP, IoU, precision/recall) and tuned hyperparameters to balance inference speed and accuracy under real-world constraints.
Moved into the final stage: integrating the model into the target environment, wrapping it in an API, and writing developer and user documentation for handover.

title: Riga Cup ⚽

events.description: Took on the Riga Cup as a freelance project and designed the overall architecture, aiming for a scalable platform for tournament and team management.
Built the backend — database schema, API endpoints, and authentication — and led a small team through the implementation.
Worked with the frontend team to integrate the API with the UI, ensuring clean data exchange between the two.
Tested the system thoroughly, fixing bugs in the tournament and team-management features with a focus on UX and performance.
Optimized performance by refining code and database queries, improving scalability and efficiency for large tournaments.
Deployed the backend to production and monitored early usage and performance to confirm stability.
